raw_text:
# 12-Week Upper-Body Programme: Right Subacromial Impingement (Below-Shoulder Loading Only)

## Before You Start

**Physio constraints:** pain-free range only, no overhead loading.

This programme keeps all loaded work **below shoulder height (under roughly 90° of flexion or abduction)**. It does not assume she will be cleared for overhead work by week 12. Phase 3 prepares her for a physio reassessment rather than progressing overhead on its own.

**Things to confirm with the physio in week 1:**
- Is she cleared to climb? Climbing is almost entirely overhead loading. If not, tell her clearly that this programme replaces climbing for now and does not supplement it. If partial climbing is allowed (e.g., low traverses with hands below the head), agree on the details in writing.
- Is there a specific range limit (e.g., 80° abduction) or a provocative position to avoid, such as internal rotation at end range?
- Is she doing a home exercise programme? Avoid duplicating rotator cuff volume, or fold her physio exercises into these sessions.
- What is the plan for reassessment around weeks 8–12?

**Pain-monitoring rule (use every session):**
- Pain of 0–2/10 during an exercise is acceptable, provided it returns to baseline within 24 hours.
- Pain of 3+/10, any sharp or pinching pain, or symptoms that are worse the next morning means: regress that exercise, reduce its range, or remove it. If symptoms persist across two sessions, refer back to the physio.
- Keep a simple log of pain score, exercise, and next-day status. It makes physio communication much easier.

**Structure:** 3 sessions per week (A, B, C) on non-consecutive days, each 50–60 minutes. Lower-body and core work is included so she keeps overall training stimulus. Add separate lower-body days if she wants them.

---

## Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Control and Tolerance

**Goals:** restore scapular control, build rotator cuff endurance, find her pain-free ranges, and establish the habit of logging.

**Loading:** light (RPE 5–6). Use slow tempo, around 3 seconds lowering. Prioritise quality over load.

**Warm-up (every session, 8–10 min):**
- Thoracic open books: 2 × 8 per side
- Foam roller thoracic extensions with hands behind the head (elbows forward, not overhead): 2 × 8
- Band pull-aparts at chest height: 2 × 15
- Scapular push-ups against a wall: 2 × 10

### Session A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Side-lying dumbbell external rotation | 3 × 12–15 | Towel under elbow, 1–2 kg |
| Chest-supported dumbbell row | 3 × 12 | Pause 1 sec at top, squeeze scapulae |
| Incline push-up (bench or bar height) | 3 × 10 | Elbows ~45°, full scapular protraction at top |
| Prone T raise (on incline bench) | 3 × 10 | Thumbs up, arms at shoulder height max |
| Goblet squat | 3 × 10 | Hold dumbbell at chest |
| Dead bug | 3 × 8 per side | Arms at 90° flexion, not further |

### Session B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Band external rotation at 0° abduction | 3 × 15 | Towel roll under arm |
| Band internal rotation at 0° abduction | 2 × 15 | Pain-free range only |
| Seated cable row (neutral grip) | 3 × 12 | Chest tall, no shrugging |
| Dumbbell floor press | 3 × 10 | Floor limits range and protects the shoulder |
| Serratus punch (supine, dumbbell) | 3 × 12 | Protract only, no elbow bend |
| Romanian deadlift | 3 × 10 | Light-moderate |
| Pallof press | 3 × 10 per side | |

### Session C
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Face pull (cable at chest height, rope) | 3 × 15 | Finish in external rotation; keep elbows below shoulder |
| Single-arm dumbbell row | 3 × 10 per side | |
| Scapular push-up (floor or incline) | 3 × 12 | |
| Farmer carry | 3 × 30 m | Shoulders packed, not shrugged |
| Wrist curl and reverse wrist curl | 2 × 15 each | Maintains forearm capacity for climbing |
| Split squat | 3 × 8 per side | |
| Side plank (from knees if needed) | 3 × 20–30 sec per side | Monitor the right shoulder in right-side plank |

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 1:** Use the lower end of the reps. Spend time finding pain-free ranges on every exercise and record any position that provokes symptoms.
- **Week 2:** Same exercises. Add 1–2 reps per set where she scored 0–1/10 pain.
- **Week 3:** Small load increases on rows and carries (+1–2 kg per dumbbell). Keep rotator cuff loads the same and add reps.
- **Week 4:** Consolidate. If all exercises are comfortable, move to the top of each rep range. Treat this as a soft check-in point, and send the physio a brief update with the pain log.

**Criteria to move to Phase 2:** all Phase 1 exercises are at 0–2/10 pain with no next-day flare, and she shows good scapular control on rows and push-ups (no winging or shrugging).

---

## Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Strength in Safe Planes

**Goals:** build pulling and pressing strength below shoulder height, increase rotator cuff load, and add more challenging scapular stability work.

**Loading:** moderate (RPE 7). Work in the 6–12 rep range for main lifts.

**Warm-up:** as Phase 1, plus 1 light set of band external rotation.

### Session A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Chest-supported row (barbell or machine) | 4 × 8 | Progressive load |
| Dumbbell bench press (flat) | 3 × 8 | Only if floor press was pain-free; stop just above chest depth if needed |
| Side-lying external rotation | 3 × 10 | Heavier than Phase 1 |
| Prone T raise | 3 × 12 | Add light dumbbells |
| Trap bar deadlift | 3 × 6 | |
| Dead bug with band resistance | 3 × 8 per side | |

### Session B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Seated cable row (wide neutral or pronated grip) | 4 × 10 | |
| Push-up (floor) or reduced incline | 3 × 8–12 | Push-up plus: extra protraction at top |
| Cable external rotation at 0° abduction | 3 × 12 | |
| Half-kneeling single-arm cable row | 3 × 10 per side | Anti-rotation core demand |
| Bulgarian split squat | 3 × 8 per side | |
| Pallof press with hold | 3 × 8 per side, 3 sec hold | |

### Session C
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Inverted row (bar at hip or chest height) | 3 × 8–10 | Hands stay well below shoulder height |
| Face pull | 3 × 15 | |
| Bear crawl | 3 × 10 m | Scapular stability under body weight |
| Suitcase carry | 3 × 30 m per side | |
| Plate pinch hold | 3 × 20–30 sec | Grip maintenance for climbing |
| Hip thrust | 3 × 10 | |
| Side plank (full) | 3 × 30 sec per side | |

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 5:** Introduce new exercises at conservative loads. Watch dumbbell bench and floor push-ups closely, since these are the most likely to provoke symptoms in this phase.
- **Week 6:** Add load to rows and carries (5–10% where reps were completed cleanly).
- **Week 7:** Add a set to the main row of each session if recovery is good. Increase rotator cuff loads gradually.
- **Week 8:** Deload. Cut volume by around 40% (drop 1–2 sets per exercise) and keep loads the same. Send the physio a progress update and ask whether a reassessment of overhead capacity is planned.

**Criteria to move to Phase 3:** stable pain scores (0–2/10) across all exercises for at least two weeks, and no flare-ups after the week 7 volume increase.

---

## Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Capacity and Physio Bridge

**Goals:** build strength and work capacity in the cleared ranges and develop rotator cuff endurance under fatigue. If the physio clears it, introduce graded movement toward higher shoulder angles.

**Loading:** moderate-heavy (RPE 7–8) on main lifts, with endurance-focused accessory work.

The programme has two tracks from here, and the physio's decision determines which one you follow.

### Track 1: No Change to Clearance (Default)
Keep all loading below shoulder height and progress volume, load, and density within the Phase 2 exercise pool.

**Session A**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Chest-supported row | 4 × 6–8 |
| Dumbbell bench press | 4 × 6–8 |
| Side-lying external rotation | 3 × 10 |
| Prone T raise | 3 × 12 |
| Trap bar deadlift | 4 × 5 |
| Ab wheel rollout (short range) | 3 × 8 |

The ab wheel rollout stops well before the arms reach overhead. Remove it if it causes any shoulder symptoms.

**Session B**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Seated cable row | 4 × 8 |
| Push-up plus | 3 × max reps (stop 2 short of failure) |
| Cable external rotation, superset with face pull | 3 × 12 + 15 |
| Single-arm dumbbell row | 3 × 8 per side |
| Front squat or goblet squat | 3 × 8 |
| Pallof press with walkout | 3 × 8 per side |

Use a goblet squat if the front squat rack position irritates the shoulder.

**Session C: Circuit**
Do 3–4 rounds with 60 seconds rest between rounds:
- Inverted row × 10
- Farmer carry × 30 m
- Bear crawl × 10 m
- Band external rotation × 15
- Plate pinch hold × 20 sec

Then finish with:
- Hip thrust 3 × 8
- Side plank 3 × 40 sec per side

### Track 2: Physio Clears Graded Progression Above Shoulder Height
Add the following only with explicit physio sign-off, and in this order. Start each one at very light loads (RPE 4–5) and keep the pain-monitoring rule in place.
1. **Wall slides** with a foam roller, progressing the height gradually
2. **Landmine press**, half-kneeling (an angled press that stops short of true overhead)
3. **Cable external rotation at 45° abduction**, then 90° if tolerated
4. **Lat pulldown**, light, in the pain-free range

Bring in only one new exercise per week. True overhead pressing and hanging (including climbing and hangboard work) stay with the physio to decide on. They are not part of this 12-week block.

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 9:** Move to Phase 3 loads. Get the physio's decision on Track 1 vs Track 2.
- **Week 10:** Progressive overload on main lifts. If on Track 2, introduce the first graded exercise.
- **Week 11:** Highest-volume week. Track the pain log closely.
- **Week 12:** Deload plus testing. Record 8RM on chest-supported row and dumbbell bench, max push-ups, and carry distances. Pass the results to the physio along with the full pain log to inform the next block.

---

## Climbing Considerations
- **Grip:** she will lose some grip conditioning if she is not climbing. The carries, pinch holds, and wrist work help, but they won't fully replicate finger strength. Tell her this so her expectations are realistic.
- **Returning to climbing:** this is the physio's call. A typical progression is low-angle traversing, then vertical routes below her grade, then steep or overhanging terrain. Hangboarding comes last.
- **Antagonist work:** the pressing and external rotation work here is worth keeping long term. Climbers are usually pull-dominant, and that imbalance can contribute to impingement.

## Office Worker Considerations
- Encourage hourly breaks: a 30-second chin tuck plus a thoracic extension over the chair back.
- Check her workstation setup. Her screen should be at eye level, and her mouse close enough that her shoulder isn't reaching forward.
- Suggest 2 × 15 band pull-aparts at her desk midday if she can keep a band at work.

## Recovery
- Allow 48 hours between upper-body sessions.
- Ask her to report sleep position. Lying on the right shoulder can aggravate impingement, so a pillow hugged in front can help her stay off it.
- If she is having a flare day, swap the session for the warm-up plus the Phase 1 rotator cuff work and lower-body exercises only.

---

**Summary:** everything here stays below shoulder height unless the physio says otherwise. Use the pain-monitoring rule every session. Keep the physio updated at weeks 4, 8, and 12. If you notice night pain, weakness, or symptoms that are getting worse, stop and refer her back.
